one_line: A text-card brand origin story over archival photos and clips: two women, presented by the on-screen 'we' as the founders, trace Slumberkins from a maternity-leave idea to hand-sewn plush to a Jim Henson Company partnership and an Apple TV+ series, ending on customer families and a thank-you.

hook.visual: Static photo of two visibly pregnant women posed side by side, inset on a dark teal background with a white serif text box above it. Frames at 0s and 2s are identical, so the first seconds have no motion.
hook.on_screen_text: The idea for Slumberkins came to us when we were both on maternity leave... (English on screen)
hook.why_it_stops_the_scroll: Inferred: an unfinished sentence ending in '...' plus a relatable parent-life image (pregnancy, maternity leave) promises an origin story. Honest read: the opening is a static photo for about 4s, so it is weak for cold viewers and stronger for existing followers. The 40x outlier probably comes from later proof points, not from this hook.

payoff: Two payoffs: the product range (books and creatures, 30-41s) and the credibility proof, a Jim Henson Company sign at 42-45s and an Apple TV+ series at 46-49s. The emotional close is customer families and a thank-you at 50-64s.
cta: None. It ends on a thank-you card ("Thanks for being part of our story. We're glad you're here") with no follow, shop or link ask on screen. The caption only says thanks.
share_or_comment_trigger: Inferred: existing followers congratulate and share a milestone post (the Jim Henson Company and Apple TV+ news at 42-49s), and parents who use the products recognise kids like their own in the final clips. 4,436 likes and 145 comments are consistent with congratulation. Shares and saves are not in meta.json.
why_it_worked: 132.9K views against an account median of 3.3K (40x). Inferred: the credibility proof at 42-49s, after a chronological build from living-room sewing at 14-19s, is what made this a milestone post. The video cannot show what the algorithm did.
Each card ends in an ellipsis and the image changes at almost every 2s frame, so one sentence is pulled across several cuts (observed 24-41s). Every cut re-opens a small loop.
3.34% like rate on 4,436 likes sits well above the 0.3% paid-promotion level, so the reach looks organic. Family clips at 52-64s give an emotional close (inferred).
paid_signal: no: like_rate_pct is 3.34, well above the 0.3 threshold, and there are no ad cues. The cause of the 40x outlier is unknown; a network share or partner reshare is possible but cannot be verified from these files.

solo_route.how: 1) Collect real assets from the founders: early photos, first sketches or prototypes, the first test print, packing the first orders, a delivered book in a family's hands, and any real press or partner proof. 2) In CapCut or Canva build 10-12 cards, one photo or short clip each, with a serif sentence box and each sentence ending in an ellipsis so it flows across cuts. 3) Follow this order: the idea, why we are qualified, the scrappy start, 'the response was overwhelming', the leap, what we make today, proof, customer families, thank-you. 4) For the 'what we make today' card, record a screen capture of the LumeBook flow where an uploaded child photo becomes the illustrated hero, using a consented photo or a team member's own childhood photo.
solo_route.needs: Founders' real photos and clips, with their consent. Written permission from any parent whose child appears. Only true proof points; no invented milestones.

lumebook_version.concept: A 45-60s origin timeline in text cards over real photos: the idea, the first test print, the first order, the first family opening their child's book, ending on a thank-you card. Use only true milestones and add a numbers card (books printed) only if it is accurate.

evidence_notes: The transcript contains only '(upbeat music)' markers at 0s, 30s and 60s, which is the only audio evidence; there is no speech, and the whole narrative is carried by on-screen English text. The two women are presented as the founders only by the on-screen 'we' and the brand name; I did not identify them further. That the Apple TV+ clip is series footage is inferred from the caption text at 46s. The tag under the plush at 18s reads 'Sleepytime Rhyme'; a second tag lower right appears to read 'SPOON & MOON' [partly unclear]. Duration 64.2s from frames/index.json. Retention is not visible; the cause of the outlier is an inference.
